questions.prompt: What kind of business is this for?
What should the website mainly do?

options.label: Run a platform customers log into

questions.prompt: Do you need any of these?

options.label: Admin panel to edit content myself

rules.architecture: Next.js or React frontend, a backend API, authentication and a database, on infrastructure sized to the workload
rules.reason: Because customers will sign in or pay, the site has to store and protect real records. That needs a backend and a database — a static website genuinely cannot do it safely.

rules.architecture: Next.js or React on Vercel with a content management workflow
rules.reason: Because you want to edit content yourself without a developer, the site needs a content system behind it. That is lighter than a full custom backend and keeps day-to-day updates in your hands.

rules.architecture: Next.js or React on Vercel, with a publishing workflow for articles
rules.reason: Publishing regularly needs a tidy way to add articles, but it does not by itself need a server or database. Articles can live as structured content and still be fast and searchable.

rules.architecture: Next.js or React on Vercel, products held as structured content, enquiries by form and WhatsApp
rules.reason: Showing a catalogue and taking enquiries does not require a server. Products can be structured content, which keeps the site fast and the running cost low. A backend is only needed once customers start buying online.

rules.architecture: Next.js or React on Vercel, connected to your own domain
rules.reason: Your site is mainly informational and does not need customer accounts or changing database content, so a managed setup keeps the architecture simple and avoids paying for a server you would not use.
